description:
TestPTYResume_NonZeroSeqSkipsAlreadySeen and similar vterm integration tests flake intermittently under full-suite -count=2 with: 'libp2p: open /mosey/pty/1.0.0: failed to negotiate protocol: protocols not supported: [/mosey/pty/1.0.0]'.

Root cause: vterm.Run does pty.StartWithSize *before* registering the /mosey/pty handler. Tests start vterm.Run in a goroutine and wait time.Sleep(100ms) before dialing. Under CPU pressure from other test packages, the fork+exec for pty.StartWithSize can take longer than 100ms, so the dial races and the server reports no handler.

Confirmed with a deliberate 250ms sleep injected before pty.StartWithSize — flake reproduces 100% in isolation, exactly mirroring the natural-load symptom.

Fix: add Options.Ready (chan<- struct{}) to vterm.Run. When non-nil, Run closes it after the three Handle calls complete. Tests pass a ready channel and block on it instead of guessing a sleep. The 6 test files that drive vterm.Run in a goroutine are updated. Production callers (cmd/mosey/launch.go) ignore the field.

Verified: 12 full-suite -count=2 stress runs after the fix, 0 failures (previously ~1-in-5).
title: Fix vterm.Run startup race exposed by -count=2 stress runs
